rationale: R7 (runtime half), the `global` literal. `extractInstanceofRefs.resolveSource` returned the string "global" when it walked past every class_declaration / function_declaration / generator_function_declaration / method_definition / variable_declarator without finding a name — i.e. for a module-scope `if (x instanceof T)` written as a bare expression statement, which is the shape line 20 pins. "global" names a symbol no file in either corpus contains. Measured on REAL JavaScript, not only on recovery residue: 14 rows across lodash's 51 ES5 files and 1 on svelte. The lane's own convention for 'this read belongs to the module' is `method || owner || moduleName`, which extractExportRelationships and the uses walk already apply. The three shapes that DO have an enclosing declaration are pinned here too, because the guard must not swallow them — a fix that returned moduleName unconditionally would pass a single forbid row and lose all four rows.

expectRelationships.note: no enclosing declaration, so the MODULE names the reference — the file's own name, the convention every other emitter here uses
a const-bound instanceof still names the binding (gap J6)
a function-bodied instanceof names the function
a method-bodied instanceof names the method, not the class

forbidRelationships.note: the placeholder literal: a symbol name no file in the corpus contains — standing rule R7
